title_he: הוֹי יוֹצֵר כָּל־בָּשָׂר, הוֹי שׁוֹכֵן מָרוֹם
review: 1:1–2 יוֹצֵר כָּל־בָּשָׂר with שׁוֹכֵן מָרוֹם — Jer 32:27 and Isa 57:15; the two titles are the Arabic's خَالِقَ الْمَلَا / سَاكِنَ الْعُلَا, and the Hebrew keeps the biblical pair rather than a modern 'Creator of people'.

1:5–8 four short denials of belonging are kept as four lines, as the Arabic has four (فَلَسْنَا مِنْ هُنَا / لَيْسَ لَنَا هَنَا / نَحْنُ الْمُزْدَرَى / لَيْسَ لَنَا وُجُود) — the repetition is the stanza's argument.
2:1 גֵּרִים — 1 Pet 2:11 (כְּגֵרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים); 'strangers' is kept as the resident-alien, not 'foreigners', because the stanza's comfort is that the exile is legal and temporary.
2:8 כּוֹכַב הַשָּׁחַר — Rev 22:16 (כּוֹכַב נֹגַהּ הַשָּׁחַר); the star is kept as a title of address, since the stanza ends by naming Him, not by describing the dawn.
3:5–8 the close is Rev 22:7 (הִנְנִי בָא מְהֵרָה) plus Rev 22:20 verbatim (אָמֵן, בּוֹאָה אֲדֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ), so the hymn ends inside the Bible's own last prayer.
4:2 כָּלְתָה לְךָ נַפְשֵׁנוּ — Ps 84:3 (נִכְסְפָה וְגַם־כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי); the bride's longing borrows the psalmist's verb instead of a modern 'we miss You'.
